title: Account Resilience Playbook — Exec Activation & Rapid Save Plays
summary: Compact, action-oriented playbook for quickly assessing renewal risk, mobilizing an execution squad, and running short-form save plays with clear escalation to execs. Designed for accounts showing mixed health signals ahead of renewal (30–90 days out).
purpose: Create a low-friction operational template that CSMs and SDRs cantrigger when a renewal is at material risk but not fully lost. Emphasis on time-boxed tactics, rapid customer signal validation, and a 48–72 hour exec activation window for high-impact accounts.
primary_objectives: 1) Objectively score renewal risk within 24 hours. 2) Run targeted mitigation plays over 7–21 days. 3) Clear handoff to execs with a one-page briefing when escalation thresholds hit. 4) Capture outcome and learning in a standard postmortem.
risk_signals:
(sample signals to watch)
- Usage drop: >30% decline in active API calls or seats week-over-week
- Feature roadmap misalignment: customer repeatedly pushes back on roadmap items tied to value metrics
- Security/compliance obstacles: stalled PoC due to SOC or legal reviews >3 weeks
- Cost complaints: repeated billing disputes or requests to pause overage charges
- Engagement signal: missed QBR, unanswered support tickets >5 days
- Competitive mention: customer evaluating publicly-known competitor or referencing case studies
- Exec churn: loss of sponsor or change in procurement owner
initial_triage_steps:
1) Validate signals (CSM): check telemetry, billing, support logs. 2) Timebox outreach: 24-hour 'status check' email + calendar. 3) Quick win search: find 1–2 low-effort fixes to restore value (config change, quota tweak, quick training session). 4) Apply risk score and route per matrix.
(Use template fields in tracking_fields below.)
risk_scoring_matrix:
Score scale: 0–10 (higher = higher risk)
- Usage: 0 (stable/ growing) | 3 (small dip) | 6 (sustained drop) | 9 (near-zero)
- Engagement: 0 (QBR done, weekly syncs) | 2 (missed 1 meeting) | 5 (missed multiple) | 8 (no contact)
- Financial: 0 (on track) | 4 (billing questions) | 7 (pause request) | 10 (payment failed/contract flagged)
- Compliance: 0 (clear) | 5 (additional review) | 9 (blocked by legal/Sec)
- Competitive: 0 (no mention) | 3 (rumor) | 6 (evaluating) | 8 (POC with competitor)
Thresholds (sum): 0–9 = low risk (monitor), 10–19 = medium (CS-led intervention), 20+ = high (exec escalation + multidisciplinary squad)
play_types:
Rapid Save Plays (pick 1–2 per account, run 7–21 days):
- Value Re-surface (1–2 days): 20-min product walkthrough focused on top 3 success metrics.
- Financial Flex (3–7 days): short-term credits, billing reclass, or trial extension with clear success criteria.
- Compliance Accelerator (7–14 days): assign security champion + dedicated legal template to unblock review.
- Exec Connect (48–72 hours): single executive-to-executive call with pre-read and ask.
- Embedded Support Blitz (3–10 days): dedicated triage channel + daily patch notes until incident resolved.
- Competitive Counterplay (7–14 days): strategic demo showing differentiators mapped to competitor objections.
Each play has a 1-line success criterion (e.g., "customer re-engaged and schedules next roadmap sync") and a rollback/timebox.
escalation_matrix:
When to escalate: aggregate score >=20 OR any single dimension >=9 OR missed resolution SLAs (see execution_timeline).
Escalation steps: 1) CS Lead notifies AM/RevOps and creates "exec-brief" doc (15–30 min). 2) If high-impact (ARR > $250k) add VP-CS and Head of Product to read-ahead. 3) Schedule Exec Connect within 48 hours (aim for 24). 4) If unresolved 72 hours after exec connect, present emergency proposal to CRO for contractual options.
Escalation outputs: one-page briefing (situation, timeline, asks), suggested mitigation options, recommended owner for each option.
Templates: use /confluence/exec-brief-template and tag slack:#cs-escalations.
execution_timeline:
T0 = risk identified.
0–24h: triage + validate signals + score.
24–48h: pick plays, assign owners, and launch outreach.
48–72h: evaluate early wins. If score remains high, prepare exec brief and request exec touch.
Day 4–14: run intervention plays, daily tracking, and customer checkpoints.
Day 15–21: decision window — renew on standard terms / concession / non-renew / extend with strict success criteria.
Post 21 days: formal churn or renewal closure, run postmortem within 10 business days.
communication_templates:
1) 24h triage email (CSM -> POA): short subject line, 3 bullets: context, immediate ask, next step. Example: 'Quick check: usage trend & next step' body: Hi <Name>, saw a drop in calls this week — can we sync 20 mins? Proposed times: X/Y. Goal: confirm value being delivered.
2) Exec brief one-pager (bullet structure): headline (1 line), impact (ARR/usage/regulatory), timeline, asks (3 max), recommended exec ask.
3) Exec connect script (30 min): 5-min intro, 10-min problem framing + data, 10-min proposed mitigation, 5-min decision/next steps.
4) Sample concession offer wording: 'We can provide a time-limited credit of $X tied to achieving Y usage by date Z.'
Full templates are in linked_artifacts repo and in Confluence template page.
tracking_fields:
(CSV-ready columns for tracker)
account_name, account_id, ARR, renewal_date, days_to_renewal, initial_score, current_score, dominant_signal, plays_launched, owners, last_customer_contact, exec_touch_date, outcome, notes_link, next_steps_deadline
Suggested dashboard tags: #save-play, #exec-activated, #financial-concession
roles_responsibilities:
CSM: lead triage, owner of customer comms, run plays.
CS Lead: approve playbook activation for medium risk, prepare exec brief.
RevOps/Finance: fast-track billing adjustments and author credit notes.
Legal/Security: expedite review using pre-approved templates.
Product/Eng: prioritize bugfixes/patches for critical platform issues under SRE rapid lane.
VP-CS / CRO: approve high-cost concessions, participate in exec connect for top-tier accounts.
decision_checklist:
Before exec escalation:
- Have we validated telemetry and billing?
- Has the CSM attempted 2 distinct engagement channels?
- Is there a clear, measurable ask for execs (yes/no)?
- Are mitigation options costed and owner-assigned?
- Is the customer ARR threshold met for exec time?
If any 'no' then remedy before escalation unless single-dimension critical (e.g., security block).
postmortem_and_followup: When a save play concludes (success or failure) create a brief postmortem: context, what we tried (plays and timeline), outcome, root causes, recommended playbook changes, and a short list of follow-up actions (owners + deadlines). Store in Confluence under /cs/postmortems and link back to account tracker.
notes_to_self: This is intentionally lean. Keep the CSM checklist printable (1 page) and ensure RevOps can commit to 48-hour billing actions. We should run a 1-hour training for CS every quarter on this flow.
related_qbr_materials: Refer to QBR one-pager templates in repo and the 'value metrics' workbook; include a 1-slide snapshot in customer QBR when play was run.
example_scenarios:
Scenario A (Mid-market dip): ARR $120k, usage -40% over 2 weeks, missing monthly syncs -> play: Value Re-surface + Financial Flex; expected 14-day window.
Scenario B (Enterprise security hold): ARR $1.2M, P0 security question blocking production -> play: Compliance Accelerator + Exec Connect; target 7–10 days.
Scenario C (Competitive churn): ARR $450k, customer in competitor POC -> play: Competitive Counterplay + Exec Connect + Embedded Support Blitz; target 14 days.
